newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Three groups drop out of Brazil's CRT shr selloff.
newsitem.headline: Three groups drop out of Brazil's CRT shr selloff.

text.p: Three of the six foreign-led groups prequalified to bid on a 35-percent stake in state-run telecom Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) have dropped out of the running, a state official said.

A spokesman for Rio Grande do Sul state said groups led by Korea Telekom, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Co and GTE Corp's GTE International Telecommunications Inc no longer plan to put forth proposals.

He did not know the reasons they bowed out and representatives of the groups were not immediately available for comment. But the consortia were prequalified before the state set a 440 million-real base price for the shares or published bid specifications.
The auction of the 35 percent of CRT's capital stock, or 262,352,653 shares, is slated for next Tuesday.
The CRT shares sale is being closely watched by the market because it kicks off the privatization of Brazil's telecoms sector, including federally owned giant Telebras.
"This will give the market an idea of what foreign investors are willing to pay for a Brazilian telecom, serving as a valuation benchmark," one analyst said.
The three remaining groups, who this week stated their commitment to bid, are:
* France Telecom with locals Banco Opportunity, Banco do Brasil and pension funds Previ, Sistel, CRT Employees Fund and Telos.
* Italy's STET and Argentina's Perez Companc S.A. with locals Camargo Correa and Bradesco.
* Telefonica Internacional de Espana of Spain with Brazil's RBS Participacoes S.A. and Cia de Telecomunicaciones de Chile, Telefonica de Argentina and Citicorp.
